questions.question: In a young adult with hyperglycemia, negative islet autoantibodies (GAD and IA-2), BMI around 25 kg/m2, glycosuria without ketoacidosis, preserved glucagon-stimulated C-peptide, and a multigenerational history of early-onset diabetes, which features most strongly support HNF1A-MODY over type 1 or type 2 diabetes at presentation?

How do you interpret a glucagon-stimulated C-peptide of 0.83 nmol/L in a newly diagnosed young adult with hyperglycemia, and how should this influence initial insulin use and subsequent de-escalation once a monogenic etiology is confirmed?
What beta-cell and renal tubular effects of HNF1A loss of function explain progressive hyperglycemia and a low renal threshold for glucose (glycosuria) in HNF1A-MODY?

When evaluating early-onset diabetes, when should you order MODY genetic testing, and how should the European-derived MODY probability calculator be interpreted or modified in non-European populations?

A novel heterozygous HNF1A missense variant (for example, p.N270S) is detected on an NGS panel in a patient with a MODY phenotype. Which ACMG criteria and supporting data (segregation, functional domain, in silico prediction, population frequency, phenotype) would you use to classify its pathogenicity?

For confirmed HNF1A-MODY, what is the preferred first-line pharmacotherapy, in whom would you favor a GLP-1 receptor agonist over a sulfonylurea, and why should SGLT2 inhibitors be used with caution in this genotype?

What is the rationale for starting basal insulin at diagnosis in some patients with very high HbA1c and suspected MODY, and what clinical or laboratory criteria support safely discontinuing insulin after confirmation of HNF1A-MODY?

After confirming HNF1A-MODY in a proband, what are best practices for cascade testing and counseling of family members, including timing of screening and implications for management if they test positive?

In a newly diagnosed young adult with diabetes who already shows markedly reduced sudomotor function on electrochemical skin conductance testing, what is the differential diagnosis for early autonomic dysfunction, and what additional evaluations would you obtain to attribute neuropathy to diabetes versus alternative causes?
Which clinical and biochemical features help distinguish HNF1A-MODY from GCK-MODY at presentation, and which findings in this case argue against GCK-MODY?
